speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a recent low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better understand your condition, how many days have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The combination of a prodromal viral illness (fever, rhinorrhea, headache) followed by a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, and specifically a facial rash sparing the perioral area, is classic for this condition. No further tests or questions are needed.
